etymology_text: Literally, “[may] the earth [be] like featherdown”; a modified calque of Latin sit tibi terra levis.

etymology_templates.name: calque
etymology_templates.expansion: calque of Latin sit tibi terra levis

examples.text: Крепко мы в те поры вздорили с покойником, господином Ворониным, ругались нещадно, — да будет ему земля пухом, хорош был мужик, стать бы ему истинным моряком, не дожил, жалко.
examples.ref: 1952, Ю. П. Герман, Россия молодая:
examples.english: Those days we had big rows with the deceased, with Mr. Voronin, we argued and did not pull any punches; may he rest in peace, a good man he was, and he would have made a true sailor, but he didn't live long enough, alas.
examples.roman: Krepko my v te pory vzdorili s pokojnikom, gospodinom Voroninym, rugalisʹ neščadno, — da budet jemu zemlja puxom, xoroš byl mužik, statʹ by jemu istinnym morjakom, ne dožil, žalko.
examples.translation: Those days we had big rows with the deceased, with Mr. Voronin, we argued and did not pull any punches; may he rest in peace, a good man he was, and he would have made a true sailor, but he didn't live long enough, alas.

examples.text: На помин души, как говорится. Земля пухом. Я протянул деньги.
examples.ref: 2001, Андрей Волос, “Недвижимость”, in Новый Мир:
examples.english: For the repose of his soul, like they say. Rest in peace. I handed over the money.
examples.roman: Na pomin duši, kak govoritsja. Zemlja puxom. Ja protjanul denʹgi.
examples.translation: For the repose of his soul, like they say. Rest in peace. I handed over the money.

examples.text: Очень заболело сердце, когда опустили Ваню, легкий, как птица, ему бы в небо, а не в землю, земля пухом, Ваня не знает, что будет ребенок от него, что ребенка никогда не будет [...]
examples.ref: 2002, Светлана Василенко, Ген смерти:
examples.english: Her heart was aching badly when they lowered Vanya down, he was as light as a bird, he should be flying up into the sky and not being put into the ground, rest in peace, Vanya doesn't know that he fathered a child, that there will never be a child …
examples.roman: Očenʹ zabolelo serdce, kogda opustili Vanju, lexkij, kak ptica, jemu by v nebo, a ne v zemlju, zemlja puxom, Vanja ne znajet, što budet rebenok ot nevo, što rebenka nikogda ne budet [...]
examples.translation: Her heart was aching badly when they lowered Vanya down, he was as light as a bird, he should be flying up into the sky and not being put into the ground, rest in peace, Vanya doesn't know that he fathered a child, that there will never be a child …

examples.text: Ещё пару лет, и это была бы мировая величина. Царство ему небесное. Земля пухом.
examples.ref: 2012, Владимир Савич, “Табуретка мира”, in Ковчег:
examples.english: Another couple years, and he would have been world-famous. May he fall asleep in the Lord. Rest in peace.
examples.roman: Ješčó paru let, i eto byla by mirovaja veličina. Carstvo jemu nebesnoje. Zemlja puxom.
examples.translation: Another couple years, and he would have been world-famous. May he fall asleep in the Lord. Rest in peace.

examples.text: Возвраща́ясь в Па́вловск уже́ в пя́том часу́ пополу́дни, он сошёлся в вокса́ле желе́зной доро́ги с Ива́ном Фёдоровичем. Тот бы́стро схвати́л его́ за́ руку, осмотре́лся круго́м, ка́к бы в испу́ге, и потащи́л кня́зя с собо́й в ваго́н пе́рвого кла́сса, чтоб е́хать вме́сте.
examples.ref: 1869, Фёдор Достоевский [Fyodor Dostoevsky], “Часть II. Глава XI”, in Идиот; English translation from Constance Garnett, transl., The Idiot, 1913:
examples.english: Returning in the afternoon, he happened upon General Epanchin at the station. The latter seized his hand, glancing around nervously, as if he were afraid of being caught in wrong-doing, and dragged him into a first-class compartment.
examples.roman: Vozvraščájasʹ v Pávlovsk užé v pjátom časú popolúdni, on sošólsja v voksále želéznoj dorógi s Ivánom Fjódorovičem. Tot býstro sxvatíl jevó zá ruku, osmotrélsja krugóm, kák by v ispúge, i potaščíl knjázja s sobój v vagón pérvovo klássa, štob jéxatʹ vméste.
examples.translation: Returning in the afternoon, he happened upon General Epanchin at the station. The latter seized his hand, glancing around nervously, as if he were afraid of being caught in wrong-doing, and dragged him into a first-class compartment.

examples.text: Вы́бежав на платфо́рму, Катю́ша то́тчас же в окне́ ваго́на пе́рвого кла́сса увида́ла его́.
examples.ref: 1899, Лев Толстой [Leo Tolstoy], “Часть I. Глава XXXVII”, in Воскресение; English translation from Louise Maude, transl., Resurrection, 1901:
examples.english: Hurrying up the platform, Katusha saw him at once at the windows of a first-class carriage.
examples.roman: Výbežav na platfórmu, Katjúša tótčas že v okné vagóna pérvovo klássa uvidála jevó.
examples.translation: Hurrying up the platform, Katusha saw him at once at the windows of a first-class carriage.

examples.text: Как бы спрова́дить его́, хоть бы э́то сто́ило не́которых изде́ржек, — вот еди́нственная мысль, кото́рая занима́ла Обло́мова.
examples.ref: 1859, Иван Гончаров [Ivan Goncharov], “Часть 3. Глава 1”, in Обломов, Санкт-Петербург: Отечественные записки; English translation from Marian Schwartz, transl., Oblomov, New York: Seven Stories Press, 2008:
examples.english: How could he send him on his way, even if doing so entailed certain costs? That was the sole thought on Oblomov’s mind.
examples.roman: Kak by sprováditʹ jevó, xotʹ by éto stóilo nékotoryx izdéržek, — vot jedínstvennaja myslʹ, kotóraja zanimála Oblómova.
examples.translation: How could he send him on his way, even if doing so entailed certain costs? That was the sole thought on Oblomov’s mind.

examples.text: —[...]Но так как мне э́ти траге́дии наску́чили вельми́, — и заме́тьте, я говорю́ серьёзно, хоть и употребля́ю славя́нские выраже́ния, — так как всё э́то вреди́т, наконе́ц, мои́м пла́нам, то я и дал себе́ сло́во спрова́дить Лебя́дкиных во что бы ни ста́ло и без ва́шего ве́дома в Петербу́рг[...]
examples.ref: 1872, Фёдор Достоевский [Fyodor Dostoevsky], “Часть 3. Глава 3. Законченный роман. II”, in Бесы; English translation from Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky, transl., Demons, Vintage Classics, 1994:
examples.english: "…But since I am exceeding weary of all these tragedies—and note that I'm speaking seriously, though I'm using antiquated expressions—since it's all finally harmful to my plans, I swore to myself I'd pack the Lebyadkins off to Petersburg at all costs and without your knowledge…"
examples.roman: —[...]No tak kak mne éti tragédii naskúčili velʹmí, — i zamétʹte, ja govorjú serʹjózno, xotʹ i upotrebljáju slavjánskije vyražénija, — tak kak vsjo éto vredít, nakonéc, moím plánam, to ja i dal sebé slóvo sprováditʹ Lebjádkinyx vo što by ni stálo i bez váševo védoma v Peterbúrg[...]
examples.translation: "…But since I am exceeding weary of all these tragedies—and note that I'm speaking seriously, though I'm using antiquated expressions—since it's all finally harmful to my plans, I swore to myself I'd pack the Lebyadkins off to Petersburg at all costs and without your knowledge…"

examples.text: По пра́вде говоря́, Пе́тенька отли́чно понима́ет, что де́ло его́ безнадёжное, что пое́здка в Головлёво принесёт то́лько ли́шние неприя́тности, но в то́м-то и шту́ка, что есть в челове́ке како́й-то тёмный инсти́нкт самосохране́ния, кото́рый переси́ливает вся́кую созна́тельность и кото́рый так и подта́лкивает: испро́буй всё до после́днего!
examples.ref: 1880, Михаил Салтыков-Щедрин [Mikhail Saltykov-Shchedrin], “Семейные итоги”, in Господа Головлёвы; English translation from I. P. Foote, transl., The Golovlevs, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1986:
examples.english: The truth is that Petenka understands perfectly well that his case is hopeless, that his journey to Golovlevo will result in nothing but more unpleasantness, but the fact of the matter is that man has in him some instinct of self-preservation which overrides all consciousness and urges him simply to carry on trying to the end.
examples.roman: Po právde govorjá, Pétenʹka otlíčno ponimájet, što délo jevó beznadjóžnoje, što pojézdka v Golovljóvo prinesjót tólʹko líšnije neprijátnosti, no v tóm-to i štúka, što jestʹ v čelovéke kakój-to tjómnyj instínkt samosoxranénija, kotóryj peresílivajet vsjákuju soznátelʹnostʹ i kotóryj tak i podtálkivajet: ispróbuj vsjo do poslédnevo!
examples.translation: The truth is that Petenka understands perfectly well that his case is hopeless, that his journey to Golovlevo will result in nothing but more unpleasantness, but the fact of the matter is that man has in him some instinct of self-preservation which overrides all consciousness and urges him simply to carry on trying to the end.

examples.text: Куст то́же мне не понра́вился: я сде́лал из него́ де́рево, из де́рева — скирд, из скирда́ — о́блако и наконе́ц так испа́чкал всю бума́гу си́ней кра́ской, что с доса́ды разорва́л её и пошёл дрема́ть на вольте́ровское кре́сло.
examples.ref: 1852, Лев Толстой [Leo Tolstoy], “Глава XI. Занятия в кабинете и гостиной”, in Детство; English translation from Charles James Hogarth, transl., Childhood, 1912:
examples.english: Yet the blue bush did not wholly please me, so I changed it into a tree, and then into a rick, until, the whole paper having now become one blur of blue, I tore it angrily in pieces, and went off to meditate in the large arm-chair.
examples.roman: Kust tóže mne ne ponrávilsja: ja sdélal iz nevó dérevo, iz déreva — skird, iz skirdá — óblako i nakonéc tak ispáčkal vsju bumágu sínej kráskoj, što s dosády razorvál jejó i pošól dremátʹ na volʹtérovskoje kréslo.
examples.translation: Yet the blue bush did not wholly please me, so I changed it into a tree, and then into a rick, until, the whole paper having now become one blur of blue, I tore it angrily in pieces, and went off to meditate in the large arm-chair.

examples.text: Она́ се́ла в своё ста́рое вольте́ровское кре́сло, поста́вив ла́мпу пода́льше на бюро́ и закры́в её колпако́м.
examples.ref: 1869, Иван Гончаров [Ivan Goncharov], “Часть V. Глава VII”, in Обрыв, Санкт-Петербург: Вестник Европы; English translation from Stephen Pearl, transl., Malinovka Heights, Alma Classics, 2020:
examples.english: She sat down in her old Voltaire armchair, moved her desk lamp a little farther away and covered it with a lampshade.
examples.roman: Oná séla v svojó stároje volʹtérovskoje kréslo, postáviv lámpu podálʹše na bjuró i zakrýv jejó kolpakóm.
examples.translation: She sat down in her old Voltaire armchair, moved her desk lamp a little farther away and covered it with a lampshade.

examples.text: Наш почте́нный хозя́ин в продолже́ние э́того разгово́ра храни́л глубо́кое молча́ние: он сиде́л с покры́тыми пле́дом нога́ми в своём глубо́ком вольте́ровском кре́сле и, по-ви́димому, ду́мал о чём-то друго́м[...]
examples.ref: 1875, Николай Лесков [Nikolai Leskov], “Глава первая”, in На краю света; English translation from Alfred Edward Chamot, transl., On the Edge of the World, 1923:
examples.english: Our respected host had remained profoundly silent during this conversation; he sat in his large arm-chair, with a plaid over his legs, and seemed to be thinking of quite other things…
examples.roman: Naš počténnyj xozjáin v prodolžénije étovo razgovóra xraníl glubókoje molčánije: on sidél s pokrýtymi plédom nogámi v svojóm glubókom volʹtérovskom krésle i, po-vídimomu, dúmal o čom-to drugóm[...]
examples.translation: Our respected host had remained profoundly silent during this conversation; he sat in his large arm-chair, with a plaid over his legs, and seemed to be thinking of quite other things…

examples.text: Оте́ц у него́ был поп, ра́но овдове́л; повенча́л каку́ю-то незако́нную сва́дьбу и был лишён ме́ста, да так, что всю жизнь пото́м не мог себе́ его́ нигде́ отыска́ть, а состоя́л при не́коей пожило́й ва́жной да́ме, кото́рая всю жизнь с ме́ста на ме́сто е́здила и, боя́сь умере́ть без покая́ния, для э́того слу́чая сего́ попа́ при себе́ вози́ла.

examples.english: His father had been a priest, who had early become a widower and was deprived of his post for having married a couple in an illegal manner, so that during the whole of his remaining life he was unable to find another, but became the chaplain of an old lady of high position, who passed her life in travelling from place to place and fearing to die without receiving the sacrament of penitence, kept this priest always with her.
examples.roman: Otéc u nevó byl pop, ráno ovdovél; povenčál kakúju-to nezakónnuju svádʹbu i byl lišón mésta, da tak, što vsju žiznʹ potóm ne mog sebé jevó nigdé otyskátʹ, a sostojál pri nékojej požilój vážnoj dáme, kotóraja vsju žiznʹ s mésta na mésto jézdila i, bojásʹ umerétʹ bez pokajánija, dlja étovo slúčaja sevó popá pri sebé vozíla.
examples.translation: His father had been a priest, who had early become a widower and was deprived of his post for having married a couple in an illegal manner, so that during the whole of his remaining life he was unable to find another, but became the chaplain of an old lady of high position, who passed her life in travelling from place to place and fearing to die without receiving the sacrament of penitence, kept this priest always with her.

examples.roman: Fákelʹščiki i grobovščikí, užé s utrá pʹjányje, s krásnymi zveropodóbnymi lícami, s poryžélymi cilíndrami na golováx, sidéli besporjádočnoj grúdoj na svoíx fórmennyx livréjax, na lošadínyx sétčatyx popónax, na tráurnyx fonarjáx i ržávymi, síplymi golosámi oráli kakúju-to neskládnuju pésnju.

examples.text: Понима́я непра́вильность разви́тия гомосексуали́ста, о́бщество не возлага́ет и не мо́жет возлага́ть вину́ за неё на носи́теля э́тих осо́бенностей. Э́тим са́мым наруша́ется в значи́тельной ме́ре та стена́, кото́рая есте́ственно воздвига́ется ме́жду гомосексуали́стом и о́бществом и заставля́ет пе́рвого глубоко́ уйти́ в себя́. Подчёркивая значе́ние исто́ков, отку́да така́я анома́лия растёт, на́ше о́бщество ря́дом профилакти́ческих и оздорови́тельных мер создаёт все необходи́мые усло́вия к тому́, что́бы жи́зненные столкнове́ния гомосексуали́стов бы́ли возмо́жно безболе́зненнее и что́бы отчуждённость, сво́йственная им, рассоса́лась в но́вом коллекти́ве.
examples.ref: 1930, Collective of authors, Great Soviet Encyclopedia: homosexuality, volume 17, pages 593–597:
examples.english: Realizing the wrong development of a homosexual, society does not and cannot lay the blame for it on the bearer of these characteristics. This violates to a large extent the wall that is naturally erected between a homosexual and society and forces the former to withdraw deeply into himself. Emphasizing the importance of the sources from which such an anomaly grows, our society creates all the necessary conditions for the life conflicts of homosexuals to be as painless as possible and for the alienation inherent in them to resolve in the new collective with a number of preventive and health-improving measures.
examples.roman: Ponimája neprávilʹnostʹ razvítija gomoseksualísta, óbščestvo ne vozlagájet i ne móžet vozlagátʹ vinú za nejó na nosítelja étix osóbennostej. Étim sámym narušájetsja v značítelʹnoj mére ta stená, kotóraja jestéstvenno vozdvigájetsja méždu gomoseksualístom i óbščestvom i zastavljájet pérvovo glubokó ujtí v sebjá. Podčórkivaja značénije istókov, otkúda takája anomálija rastjót, náše óbščestvo rjádom profilaktíčeskix i ozdorovítelʹnyx mer sozdajót vse neobxodímyje uslóvija k tomú, štóby žíznennyje stolknovénija gomoseksualístov býli vozmóžno bezboléznenneje i štóby otčuždjónnostʹ, svójstvennaja im, rassosálasʹ v nóvom kollektíve.
examples.translation: Realizing the wrong development of a homosexual, society does not and cannot lay the blame for it on the bearer of these characteristics. This violates to a large extent the wall that is naturally erected between a homosexual and society and forces the former to withdraw deeply into himself. Emphasizing the importance of the sources from which such an anomaly grows, our society creates all the necessary conditions for the life conflicts of homosexuals to be as painless as possible and for the alienation inherent in them to resolve in the new collective with a number of preventive and health-improving measures.

examples.translation: "What is it you want, sir?" she asked, continuing her occupation.

examples.text:
Произошла́ па́уза, по́сле кото́рой, сде́лав над собо́й страшне́йшее уси́лие, Стёпа вы́говорил:
– Что вам уго́дно? – и сам порази́лся, не узна́в своего́ го́лоса. Сло́во «что» он произнёс диска́нтом, «вам» – ба́сом, а «уго́дно» у него́ совсе́м не вы́шло.
examples.ref: 1973, Михаил Булгаков [Mikhail Bulgakov], “Глава VII. Нехорошая квартирка”, in Мастер и Маргарита; English translation from Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky, transl., Master and Margarita, London: Penguin Books, 1997:
examples.english:
There was a pause, after which, making a most terrible strain on himself, Styopa uttered:
‘What can I do for you?’ - and was amazed, not recognizing his own voice. He spoke the word ‘what’ in a treble, ‘can I’ in a bass, and his ‘do for you’ did not come off at all.
examples.roman:
Proizošlá páuza, pósle kotóroj, sdélav nad sobój strašnéjšeje usílije, Stjópa výgovoril:
– Što vam ugódno? – i sam porazílsja, ne uznáv svojevó gólosa. Slóvo «što» on proiznjós diskántom, «vam» – básom, a «ugódno» u nevó sovsém ne výšlo.
examples.translation:
There was a pause, after which, making a most terrible strain on himself, Styopa uttered:
‘What can I do for you?’ - and was amazed, not recognizing his own voice. He spoke the word ‘what’ in a treble, ‘can I’ in a bass, and his ‘do for you’ did not come off at all.

examples.text: Beſides theſe two Gentlemen, and Secretaries that order the whole Citie, there are Staruſts or Aldermen for euerie ſeuerall companie. The Alderman hath his Sotskey or Conſtable, and the Conſtable hath certeine Decetskeis or Decurions vnder him, which haue the ouerſight of ten houſholds a peece, whereby euerie diſorder is ſooner ſpide, and the common ſeruice hath the quicker diſpach. The whole number of Citizens poore and rich are reduced into companies. The chiefe officers (as the Dyacks and Gentlemen) are appointed by the Emperour himſelfe, the Staruſt by the Gentlemen and Dyacks, the Sotskoy by the Staruſt or Alderman, and the Decetskotes by the Conſtables.

examples.text: А ты, дорогая Ниса, обладай мною вечно, ежели я обладания твоего достоин. О Ниса! Ниса! Ты мне милее света очей моих, не променяю тебя я на все сокровища земные и на всё счастие человеческое.
examples.ref: 1765, A. P. Sumarokov, chapter XV, in Guardian:
examples.english: And you, dear Nisa, possess me forever, if I am worthy of your possession. O Nisa! Nisa! You are dearer to me than the light of my eyes, I would not exchange you for all the treasures of the earth and for all the happiness of man.
examples.roman: A ty, dorogaja Nisa, obladaj mnoju večno, ježeli ja obladanija tvojevo dostoin. O Nisa! Nisa! Ty mne mileje sveta očej moix, ne promenjaju tebja ja na vse sokrovišča zemnyje i na vsjo sčastije čelovečeskoje.
examples.translation: And you, dear Nisa, possess me forever, if I am worthy of your possession. O Nisa! Nisa! You are dearer to me than the light of my eyes, I would not exchange you for all the treasures of the earth and for all the happiness of man.

examples.text:
Подай пepо — пишу — хочу на свете жить, Чтоб Нису мне любить. А ты к тому пpибавь: хочу его любить, Чтоб мог он жить.
Podaj pepo — pišu — xoču na svete žitʹ, Štob Nisu mne ljubitʹ. A ty k tomu pribavʹ: xoču jevo ljubitʹ, Štob mog on žitʹ.
examples.ref: 1807, V. L. Pushkin, Treaty with Nisa
examples.english: Give me a pen — I'm writing — I want to live in this world, So that I can love Nisa. And you add to that: I want to love him, So that he can live.

examples.text: По́мню, как одна́жды Ната́ша, наслу́шавшись на́ших разгово́ров, таи́нственно отвела́ меня́ в сто́рону и со слеза́ми умоля́ла поду́мать о мое́й судьбе́, допра́шивала меня́, выпы́тывала: что я и́менно де́лаю, и, когда́ я пе́ред ней не откры́лся, взяла́ с меня́ кля́тву, что я не сгублю́ себя́ как лентя́й и праздношата́йка.
examples.ref: 1861, Фёдор Достоевский [Fyodor Dostoevsky], “Часть I. Глава V”, in Униженные и оскорблённые; English translation from Constance Garnett, transl., The Insulted and Humiliated, London: Heinemann, 1915:
examples.english: I remember that one day Natasha, overhearing our conversation, drew me aside mysteriously and besought me with tears to think of my future. She kept questioning me and trying to discover what I was doing, and when I refused to tell my secret even to her, she made me swear that I would not ruin myself by being an idler and a loafer.
examples.roman: Pómnju, kak odnáždy Natáša, naslúšavšisʹ nášix razgovórov, taínstvenno otvelá menjá v stóronu i so slezámi umoljála podúmatʹ o mojéj sudʹbé, doprášivala menjá, vypýtyvala: što ja ímenno délaju, i, kogdá ja péred nej ne otkrýlsja, vzjalá s menjá kljátvu, što ja ne sgubljú sebjá kak lentjáj i prazdnošatájka.
examples.translation: I remember that one day Natasha, overhearing our conversation, drew me aside mysteriously and besought me with tears to think of my future. She kept questioning me and trying to discover what I was doing, and when I refused to tell my secret even to her, she made me swear that I would not ruin myself by being an idler and a loafer.

examples.translation: She skated a little uncertainly; taking her hands out of the little muff that hung on a cord, she held them ready for emergency, and looking towards Levin, whom she had recognized, she smiled at him, and at her own fears.

etymology_text: Ultimately from Ancient Greek ἔκκεντρος (ékkentros); suffixed with -ический (-ičeskij). By surface analysis, экс- (eks-) + центри́ческий (centríčeskij).

examples.text: Его́ ка́рие, с желтизно́й, больши́е, вырази́тельные глаза́ ме́дленно посма́тривали круго́м, то слегка́ прищу́риваясь от со́лнца, то вдруг упо́рно провожа́я каку́ю-нибудь ми́мо проходи́вшую эксцентри́ческую фигу́ру, причём бы́страя, почти́ де́тская усме́шка чуть-чу́ть тро́гала его́ то́нкие усы́, гу́бы и выдаю́щийся круто́й подборо́док.
examples.ref: 1867, Иван Тургенев [Ivan Turgenev], “II”, in Дым; English translation from Constance Garnett, transl., Smoke, 1896:
examples.english: His large expressive golden-brown eyes were gazing deliberately about him, sometimes screwed up to keep the sunshine out of them, and then watching fixedly some eccentric figure that passed by him, while a childlike smile faintly stirred his fine moustache and lips, and his prominent short chin.
examples.roman: Jevó kárije, s želtiznój, bolʹšíje, vyrazítelʹnyje glazá médlenno posmátrivali krugóm, to slexká priščúrivajasʹ ot sólnca, to vdrug upórno provožája kakúju-nibudʹ mímo proxodívšuju ekscentríčeskuju figúru, pričóm býstraja, počtí détskaja usméška čutʹ-čútʹ trógala jevó tónkije usý, gúby i vydajúščijsja krutój podboródok.
examples.translation: His large expressive golden-brown eyes were gazing deliberately about him, sometimes screwed up to keep the sunshine out of them, and then watching fixedly some eccentric figure that passed by him, while a childlike smile faintly stirred his fine moustache and lips, and his prominent short chin.

examples.text: Между тѣмъ и Новгородцы показались на Ладожскомъ озерѣ, однакоже слишкомъ поздно для дальнѣйшаго предприятїя: они возвратились назадъ, пустя на неприятеля Ижоръ, которые встрѣтя бѣгущихъ побили изъ нихъ множество, а остальныхъ прогнали.
examples.ref: 1819, Изследования служащие к объяснению древней Русской Истории [An investigation serving as the explanation of the ancient Russian History], pages 113-114:
examples.english: In the meantime the Novgorodians appeared at lake Ladoga, but too late for the following event: they returned, sending Izhorians against the enemy, who, having found those who fled, killed a majority of them, and the rest they chased away.
examples.roman: Meždu těm i Novgorodcy pokazalisʹ na Ladožskom ozerě, odnakože sliškom pozdno dlja dalʹnějšago predprijatija: oni vozvratilisʹ nazad, pustja na neprijatelja Ižor, kotoryje vstrětja běguščix pobili iz nix množestvo, a ostalʹnyx prognali.
examples.translation: In the meantime the Novgorodians appeared at lake Ladoga, but too late for the following event: they returned, sending Izhorians against the enemy, who, having found those who fled, killed a majority of them, and the rest they chased away.

examples.text: Можно даже предпологать, что между карелами, крещенными Ярославомъ, было много ижоръ, хотя ижоры, въ полномъ своемъ составѣ, приняли христіанство позднѣе.
examples.ref: 1875, Историко-статистическия свѣдѣния о С.-Петербургской епархии [Historically-statistical data on the Saint Petersburg diocese], page 19:
examples.english: It can even be suggested that among the Karelians that were christianised by Yaroslav there were many Izhorians, even though Izhorians as a whole took on Christianity later.
examples.roman: Možno daže predpologatʹ, što meždu karelami, kreščennymi Jaroslavom, bylo mnogo ižor, xotja ižory, v polnom svojem sostavě, prinjali xristianstvo pozdněje.
examples.translation: It can even be suggested that among the Karelians that were christianised by Yaroslav there were many Izhorians, even though Izhorians as a whole took on Christianity later.

examples.text: Сегодня у потомков финнов и ижор есть также русские (или иные) корни – так что, в общем, мало оснований считать этих людей финнами или ижорами.
examples.ref: 2014, “Финны, ижоры и симулякры [Finns, Izhorians and simulacra]”, in Inkeri, volume 82, number 2, page 12:
examples.english: Nowadays the descendants of Finns and Izhorians also have Russian (or other) roots, and so all in all there is little reason to consider these people Finns or Izhorians.
examples.roman: Sevodnja u potomkov finnov i ižor jestʹ takže russkije (ili inyje) korni – tak što, v obščem, malo osnovanij sčitatʹ etix ljudej finnami ili ižorami.
examples.translation: Nowadays the descendants of Finns and Izhorians also have Russian (or other) roots, and so all in all there is little reason to consider these people Finns or Izhorians.

examples.text: Кро́ме э́тих поимено́ванных лиц, ру́сских и иностра́нцев (в осо́бенности иностра́нцев, кото́рые с сме́лостью, сво́йственною лю́дям в де́ятельности среди́ чужо́й среды́, ка́ждый день предлага́ли но́вые неожи́данные мы́сли), бы́ло ещё мно́го лиц второсте́пенных, находи́вшихся при а́рмии потому́, что тут бы́ли их принципа́лы.
examples.ref: 1869, Лев Толстой [Leo Tolstoy], “Том 3, Часть первая, IX”, in Война и мир; English translation from Aylmer and Louise Maude, transl., War and Peace, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1922–1923:

examples.translation: Besides these Russians and foreigners who propounded new and unexpected ideas every day—especially the foreigners, who did so with a boldness characteristic of people employed in a country not their own—there were many secondary personages accompanying the army because their principals were there.

examples.translation: What was the meaning of this fantastic mood? head_templates.name: ru-noun+
head_templates.expansion: полти́на • (poltína) f inan (genitive полти́ны, nominative plural полти́ны, genitive plural полти́н, relational adjective полти́нный)

etymology_text:
Inherited from Old East Slavic полтина (poltina), which is attested in early 12th century. Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *polъ (“half”), but the exact derivation is uncertain; there are multiple hypotheses:
* A suffixed derivation of Old East Slavic полъть (polŭtĭ, “half of an animal carcass”).
* Derived from Proto-Slavic *polъ (“half”) + *tęti (“to chop”), perhaps referring to a one-ruble silver ingot chopped in half; compare typologically рубль (rublʹ) (akin to руби́ть (rubítʹ))) and English shilling (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kelH-).
* From Old East Slavic полъ (polŭ, “half”) + -ина (-ina), with the epenthetic -т- modeled on numeric fraction terms such as Old East Slavic десѧтина (desętina).
* From Old East Slavic полъ (polŭ, “half”) + a currency term derived from Proto-Turkic *tegiŋ (compare modern Russian тин (tin)). Dobrodomov favors this hypothesis on the grounds that none of the others can explain the Old East Slavic form полтына (poltyna), which is also found in 12th century sources.

examples.roman: Tut Razumíxin prinjalsjá razvivátʹ svoj projékt i mnógo tolkovál o tom, kak počtí vse náši knigoprodávcy i izdáteli málo znájut tólku v svojóm továre, a potomú obyknovénno i ploxíje izdáteli, meždu tém kak porjádočnyje izdánija voobščé okupájutsja i dajút procént, inogdá značítelʹnyj.
examples.translation: Then Razumihin began to unfold his project, and he explained at length that almost all our publishers and booksellers know nothing at all of what they are selling, and for that reason they are usually bad publishers, and that any decent publications pay as a rule and give a profit, sometimes a considerable one.

examples.english: What was extraordinary was that everyone not only liked him, but even people previously unsympathetic, cold, and callous, were enthusiastic over him, gave way to him in everything, treated his feeling with tenderness and delicacy, and shared his conviction that he was the happiest man in the world because his betrothed was beyond perfection.

examples.translation: What was extraordinary was that everyone not only liked him, but even people previously unsympathetic, cold, and callous, were enthusiastic over him, gave way to him in everything, treated his feeling with tenderness and delicacy, and shared his conviction that he was the happiest man in the world because his betrothed was beyond perfection.

examples.text: — С тех по́р, госуда́рь мой, — продолжа́л он по́сле не́которого молча́ния, — с тех по́р, по одному́ неблагоприя́тному слу́чаю и по донесе́нию неблагонаме́ренных лиц, — чему́ осо́бенно спосо́бствовала Да́рья Фра́нцевна, за то бу́дто бы, что ей в надлежа́щем почте́нии манки́ровали, — с тех по́р дочь моя́, Со́фья Семёновна, жёлтый биле́т принуждена́ была́ получи́ть, и уже́ вме́сте с на́ми по слу́чаю сему́ не могла́ остава́ться. [...]
examples.ref: 1866, Фёдор Достоевский [Fyodor Dostoevsky], “Часть I, Глава II”, in Преступление и наказание, Москва: Русский вестник; English translation from Constance Garnett, transl., Crime and Punishment, 1914:
examples.english: "Since then, sir," he went on after a brief pause—"Since then, owing to an unfortunate occurrence and through information given by evil-intentioned persons—in all which Darya Frantsovna took a leading part on the pretext that she had been treated with want of respect—since then my daughter Sofya Semyonovna has been forced to take a yellow ticket, and owing to that she is unable to go on living with us. …"
examples.roman: — S tex pór, gosudárʹ moj, — prodolžál on pósle nékotorovo molčánija, — s tex pór, po odnomú neblagoprijátnomu slúčaju i po doneséniju neblagonamérennyx lic, — čemú osóbenno sposóbstvovala Dárʹja Fráncevna, za to búdto by, što jej v nadležáščem počténii mankírovali, — s tex pór dočʹ mojá, Sófʹja Semjónovna, žóltyj bilét prinuždená bylá polučítʹ, i užé vméste s námi po slúčaju semú ne moglá ostavátʹsja. [...]
examples.translation: "Since then, sir," he went on after a brief pause—"Since then, owing to an unfortunate occurrence and through information given by evil-intentioned persons—in all which Darya Frantsovna took a leading part on the pretext that she had been treated with want of respect—since then my daughter Sofya Semyonovna has been forced to take a yellow ticket, and owing to that she is unable to go on living with us. …"

examples.text: Она́ хоте́ла бы́ло жить одна́ на кварти́ре, но ей не позво́лили. И около́точный сказа́л ей, что она́ мо́жет жить так, то́лько получи́в жёлтый биле́т и подчини́вшись осмо́тру.
examples.ref: 1899, Лев Толстой [Leo Tolstoy], “Часть I. Глава II”, in Воскресение; English translation from Louise Maude, transl., Resurrection, 1901:
examples.english: She meant to continue living in the lodging by herself, but was informed by the police that in this case she would have to get a license.
examples.roman: Oná xotéla býlo žitʹ odná na kvartíre, no jej ne pozvólili. I okolótočnyj skazál jej, što oná móžet žitʹ tak, tólʹko polučív žóltyj bilét i podčinívšisʹ osmótru.
examples.translation: She meant to continue living in the lodging by herself, but was informed by the police that in this case she would have to get a license.

examples.text: Де́вушка там произвела́ благоприя́тное впечатле́ние, и в то́т же день её па́спорт был сменён в поли́ции на так называ́емый жёлтый биле́т.
examples.ref: 1909–1915, Александр Куприн [Aleksandr I. Kuprin], “Часть вторая, III”, in Яма; English translation from Bernard Guilbert Guerney, transl., The Pit, (Please provide a date or year):
examples.english: The girl made a favourable impression there, and that same day her passport was changed by the police to a so-called yellow ticket.
examples.roman: Dévuška tam proizvelá blagoprijátnoje vpečatlénije, i v tót že denʹ jejó pásport byl smenjón v polícii na tak nazyvájemyj žóltyj bilét.
examples.translation: The girl made a favourable impression there, and that same day her passport was changed by the police to a so-called yellow ticket.

examples.text: — Да, тебе́ интере́сно. Но мне интере́с уж друго́й, чем тебе́. examples.ref: 1877, Лев Толстой [Leo Tolstoy], “Часть VII. Глава VIII”, in Анна Каренина; English translation from Constance Garnett, transl., Anna Karenina, 1901:
examples.english: "Yes, it's interesting for you. But its interest for me is quite different. You look at those little old men now," he said, pointing to a club member with bent back and projecting lip, shuffling towards them in his soft boots, "and imagine that they were shlupiks like that from their birth up."
examples.roman: — Da, tebé interésno. No mne interés už drugój, čem tebé. Ty vot smótrišʹ na étix staričkóv, — skazál on, ukázyvaja na sgórblennovo čléna s otvísloju gubój, kotóryj, čutʹ peredvigája nógi v mjáxkix sapogáx, prošól im navstréču, — i dúmaješʹ, što oní tak rodílisʹ šljúpikami.
examples.translation: "Yes, it's interesting for you. But its interest for me is quite different. You look at those little old men now," he said, pointing to a club member with bent back and projecting lip, shuffling towards them in his soft boots, "and imagine that they were shlupiks like that from their birth up."

examples.text: О́ба вы́сунули свои́ го́ловы из окна́ и глядя́т в сто́рону на воро́та, о́коло кото́рых на ла́вочке сиди́т домохозя́ин Ляшкевского, пу́хленький обыва́тель в расстёгнутой жиле́тке, в широ́ких си́них пантало́нах и с отви́слыми по́тными щёчками.
examples.ref: 1887, Антон Чехов [Anton Chekhov], Обыватели; English translation from Constance Garnett, transl., Aborigines, 1922:
examples.english: Both have thrust their heads out of the window, and are looking in the direction of the gate near which Lyashkevsky's landlord, a plump little native with pendulous perspiring cheeks, in full, blue trousers, is sitting on a bench with his waistcoat unbuttoned.
examples.roman: Óba výsunuli svoí gólovy iz okná i gljadját v stóronu na voróta, ókolo kotóryx na lávočke sidít domoxozjáin Ljaškevskovo, púxlenʹkij obyvátelʹ v rasstjógnutoj žilétke, v širókix sínix pantalónax i s otvíslymi pótnymi ščóčkami.
examples.translation: Both have thrust their heads out of the window, and are looking in the direction of the gate near which Lyashkevsky's landlord, a plump little native with pendulous perspiring cheeks, in full, blue trousers, is sitting on a bench with his waistcoat unbuttoned.

etymology_text: Inherited from Old East Slavic Тъмуторокань (Tŭmutorokanĭ), which is borrowed from Byzantine Greek (compare Ταματάρχα (Tamatárkha)), which is likely derived from the native Adyghe (Circassian) toponym Тамэтӏаркъу (Tamɛtʼarqʷu). The Russian spelling is the result of a folk etymology that altered the word to fit the native Russian words тьма (tʹma, “darkness”) and тарака́н (tarakán, “cockroach”) (literally "dark cockroach").

examples.text: Именно Марсель Дюшан являлся для подсудимого высшим феноменом человеческой культуры всех эпох. Почему? Не могу ответить вразумительно. Ведь были же и другие имена, и не хуже: Шекспир, к примеру, тот же Леонардо, на худой случай — Гёте. Или Платон. Тоже ведь не хуй собачий. Но для подсудимого — Дюшан, и хоть ты заебись берёзовой палкой!
examples.ref: 1983, Vladimir Sorokin, Норма (overall work in Russian):
examples.english: Marcel Duchamp of all people was for the defendant the supreme phenomenon of human culture of all time. Why? I can’t answer rationally. After all, there were other names just as significant, if not more so: Shakespeare, for instance, or the well-known Leonardo, or—at a pinch—Goethe. Or Plato. Not a slouch either after all. But for the defendant, it was Duchamp—and it wouldn't change even if you fucked yourself with a birch stick!
examples.roman: Imenno Marselʹ Djušan javljalsja dlja podsudimovo vysšim fenomenom čelovečeskoj kulʹtury vsex epox. Počemu? Ne mogu otvetitʹ vrazumitelʹno. Vedʹ byli že i drugije imena, i ne xuže: Šekspir, k primeru, tot že Leonardo, na xudoj slučaj — Gjóte. Ili Platon. Tože vedʹ ne xuj sobačij. No dlja podsudimovo — Djušan, i xotʹ ty zajebisʹ berjózovoj palkoj!
examples.translation: Marcel Duchamp of all people was for the defendant the supreme phenomenon of human culture of all time. Why? I can’t answer rationally. After all, there were other names just as significant, if not more so: Shakespeare, for instance, or the well-known Leonardo, or—at a pinch—Goethe. Or Plato. Not a slouch either after all. But for the defendant, it was Duchamp—and it wouldn't change even if you fucked yourself with a birch stick!

examples.text:
— А где бы тут обсуши́ться? Самова́р у кого́-нибудь на дере́вне есть?
— Как не быть самова́ров, — с ва́жностью возрази́л ма́лый в се́ром кафта́не, — ступа́йте к отцу́ Тимофе́ю, а не то в дворо́вую избу́, а не то к Наза́ру Тара́сычу, а не то к Аграфе́не-пти́шнице.
— С кем ты э́то говори́шь, болва́н ты э́такой? спать не даёшь, болва́н! — разда́лся го́лос из сосе́дней ко́мнаты.
— А вот господи́н како́й-то зашёл, спра́шивает, где бы обсуши́ться.
examples.ref: 1847, Иван Тургенев [Ivan Turgenev], Контора; English translation from Constance Garnett, transl., The Counting-House, 1895:
examples.english:
'Where could I dry my clothes here? Is there a samovar anywhere in the village?'
'Samovars, of course,' replied the young man in the grey coat with dignity; 'go to Father Timofey's, or to the servants' cottage, or else to Nazar Tarasitch, or to Agrafena, the poultry-woman.'
'Who are you talking to, you blockhead? Can't you let me sleep, dummy!' shouted a voice from the next room.
'Here's a gentleman's come in to ask where he can dry himself.'
examples.roman:
— A gde by tut obsušítʹsja? Samovár u kovó-nibudʹ na derévne jestʹ?
— Kak ne bytʹ samovárov, — s vážnostʹju vozrazíl mályj v sérom kaftáne, — stupájte k otcú Timoféju, a ne to v dvoróvuju izbú, a ne to k Nazáru Tarásyču, a ne to k Agraféne-ptíšnice.
— S kem ty éto govoríšʹ, bolván ty étakoj? spatʹ ne dajóšʹ, bolván! — razdálsja gólos iz sosédnej kómnaty.
— A vot gospodín kakój-to zašól, sprášivajet, gde by obsušítʹsja.
examples.translation:
'Where could I dry my clothes here? Is there a samovar anywhere in the village?'
'Samovars, of course,' replied the young man in the grey coat with dignity; 'go to Father Timofey's, or to the servants' cottage, or else to Nazar Tarasitch, or to Agrafena, the poultry-woman.'
'Who are you talking to, you blockhead? Can't you let me sleep, dummy!' shouted a voice from the next room.
'Here's a gentleman's come in to ask where he can dry himself.'

examples.text:
— Здесь не ме́сто петь, — с твёрдостию возрази́л Куприя́н, — здесь госпо́дская конто́ра.
— Да тебе́-то что за де́ло? Чай, в конто́рщики сам ме́тишь! — с гру́бым сме́хом отвеча́л Константи́н. — Должно́ быть!
examples.ref: 1847, Иван Тургенев [Ivan Turgenev], Контора; English translation from Constance Garnett, transl., The Counting-House, 1895:
examples.english:
'This is not the place to sing,' Kuprya replied firmly; 'this is the manor counting-house.'
'And what's that to do with you? you've got your eye on a place as clerk, eh?' answered Konstantin with a coarse laugh. 'That's what it is!'
examples.roman:
— Zdesʹ ne mésto petʹ, — s tvjórdostiju vozrazíl Kupriján, — zdesʹ gospódskaja kontóra.
— Da tebé-to što za délo? Čaj, v kontórščiki sam métišʹ! — s grúbym sméxom otvečál Konstantín. — Dolžnó bytʹ!

'This is not the place to sing,' Kuprya replied firmly; 'this is the manor counting-house.'
